_comment: Scans that show more than the work: the picture frame, a miniature's case, a mount. Keyed '<folder>/<filename>'. l/t/r/b: percent of the displayed original (after EXIF rotation) cut from the left, top, right and bottom. The original stays the Commons file; shrink-sources, build-tiles and build-data apply the cut (scripts/lib/scan-crops.mjs). Editing an entry makes the cropped works' variants and tiles stale: rerun assets:shrink, assets:build-data and assets:tiles with --only for them. Measured on the 1280 variant and checked by eye on 17 October 2026; Rico approved each from before/after proofs. 'panels' lists the panels of a polyptych photographed as one object, x0/y0/x1/y1 in percent of the cut image, left to right; with panelCm (each panel bare, width and height), frameCm and gapCm (0 where the wings are hinged); the museum hangs each panel in its own frame at those sizes.

collection-of-beauty/La_caída_de_Faetón_._why: the scan shows its picture frame (The Fall of Phaethon, None)

collection-of-beauty/Queensland_Art_Gall._why: the scan shows a flat surround round the picture (Figure with Snow Falling, Takahashi Shōtei)

collection-of-beauty/Franz_von_Stuck_Sal._why: the scan shows the frame Stuck designed for it (Salome, Franz von Stuck); the museum builds that frame again round the cut canvas (frame-design.ts, PINNED_FRAMES)

collection-of-beauty/El_jardín_de_las_D._why: triptych, open; the scan shows the outer frame and the frames between the panels (The Garden of Earthly Delights, Hieronymus Bosch)
collection-of-beauty/El_jardín_de_las_D._sizes: Prado: overall 205.5 × 384.9 cm; framed centre 220 × 195 and wing 220 × 97.5 (Wikipedia, after the Prado). Bare panels 172.5 and 76.5 × 185.8 cm; the frames, black with gilt fillets on the scan, are 11 cm (195 − 172.5 = 22.5, and 22 cm between panels on the scan). The wings are hinged: no gap.

collection-of-beauty/Hieronymus_Bosch_-_._why: the closed wings of the Garden of Earthly Delights, two panels in their frames (Creation, Hieronymus Bosch)
collection-of-beauty/Hieronymus_Bosch_-_._sizes: The Garden's wings closed: the same two panels and frames as the open triptych.

collection-of-beauty/Rogier_van_der_Weyd._why: triptych; the scan shows the outer frame and the frames between the panels (Crucifixion Triptych, Rogier van der Weyden)
collection-of-beauty/Rogier_van_der_Weyd._sizes: KHM 901 (khm.at/en/object/2123): middle panel 96 × 69 cm, wings 96 × 27 cm, wing framed 101 × 35 cm, so 4 cm frames. On the scan a dark hinge gap of about 2 cm stands between the gilt frames.

collection-of-beauty/Hieronymus_Bosch_-_._why: triptych photographed as three panels on a white ground (Triptych of the Temptation of St Anthony, Hieronymus Bosch)
collection-of-beauty/Hieronymus_Bosch_-_._sizes: MNAA: overall 131.5 × 238 cm; centre 119 and wings 53 cm wide. The scan shows no frames: 8 cm frames and hinged wings are chosen, not measured.

collection-of-beauty/Albrecht_Dürer_-_Ad._why: diptych, two panels on a white ground (Adam and Eve, Albrecht Dürer)
collection-of-beauty/Albrecht_Dürer_-_Ad._sizes: Prado: Adam 209 × 81 cm, Eve 209 × 80 cm, two pictures in two frames hung side by side. The scan shows no frames: 8 cm frames and a 20 cm gap are chosen, not measured.

collection-of-beauty/Hugo_van_der_Goes_-._why: diptych, two panels side by side (Vienna Diptych, Hugo van der Goes)
collection-of-beauty/Hugo_van_der_Goes_-._sizes: KHM: Fall of Man 33.8 × 22.9 cm, framed 41 × 30.5 cm, mounted with the Lamentation 61.5 cm wide: 3.8 cm frames and 0.5 cm between them.
